author: Maya Yang
description:
In 2024 ethics filing, US health secretary pledged to ‘not engage in writing, editing, marketing or promotional services for any of these books during government service’

Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, received $4m over the last year in book advances from allies within the Make America Healthy Again movement, according to a new report.

The advances were for upcoming books by Skyhorse Publishing, a publishing house belonging to Tony Lyons, a friend of Kennedy Jr who is also president of Maha Center, a non-profit that describes itself as “tackling America’s health crisis through education, investigation, innovation and action”.

Continue reading...
title: RFK Jr received $4m in book advances from Maha allies over past year

author: Ariana Baio in Washington
description:
US president to give red-carpet treatment to Chinese counterpart despite tensions over AI development

  • Trump greets Xi – live updates

  • AI looms large over Trump-Xi meeting amid US-China distrust

Donald Trump welcomed Xi Jinping to the US on Wednesday evening at the tarmac at Joint Base Andrews, an unusually generous meeting to kick off the Chinese president’s state visit.

For the world leaders’ second meeting this year, the US president is expected to roll out the red carpet for his Chinese counterpart as top issues such as the race in artificial intelligence development and geopolitical instability loom.
title: Trump greets Xi Jinping at plane as Chinese leader arrives for state visit

author: Chris Stein
description:
Republican senator calls bribery allegation ‘categorically false’ as ProPublica reports Trump derailed FBI inquiry

Democrats in Maine on Wednesday accused Republican senator Susan Collins of corruption after a major media outlet reported that the FBI had proposed investigating her for allegedly accepting bribes – before Donald Trump derailed the inquiry.

The article from the investigative newsroom ProPublica rocked the race for Collins’s Senate seat, which is crucial to Democrats’ hopes of winning control of the chamber in the 3 November midterm election. The outlet reported that in the run-up to Collins’s successful bid for a fifth term in 2020, the head of her Super Pac had solicited a campaign donation from contracting firm Navatek, which demanded assurances of business from the government in return.

Continue reading...
title: Democrats accuse Susan Collins of corruption after bombshell ‘pay-to-play’ report

author: Lois Beckett
description:
Scientists are questioning whether the nestings on Seal and Huntington Beach were freak occurrences or start of a trend

A sea turtle crawled out of the surf in southern California last weekend around sunset and started laying eggs in the sand.

People on Huntington Beach who saw the female olive ridley sea turtle were shocked and excited. And they weren’t the only ones freaking out, said Justin Viezbicke, the California stranding coordinator for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Association (Noaa).

Continue reading...
title: In a first, olive ridley turtles spotted nesting on California’s beaches

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

In a busy day of dipolomacy, Anthony Albanese also announced Australia will provide $60m more in support for Ukraine’s fight against Russia’s invasion as part of a fresh security agreement, Australian Associated Press reports.

The prime minister met Ukraine’s president, Volodymyr ⁠Zelenskyy, on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.

This is an issue not just for Europe, this is an issue for the world. If a large, more powerful country in Russia is allowed to profit from breaking the international rules of law with its illegal and immoral invasion of Ukraine, then that sets a bad precedent for the entire world.
title: Australia news live: Anthony Albanese says OpenAI agent hacked Medicare

author: Pippa Crerar and Tom Garry
description:
Prime minister says measure is discriminatory when fans of other sports are not similarly restricted

Andy Burnham has signalled he may lift the ban on drinking alcohol in the stands at football matches, suggesting it is “unfair” for fans to be singled out when it is permitted for other sports.

The prime minister, a committed Everton fan who still attends matches, said there was a case for trialling an end to the ban to bring football in line with rugby and cricket.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham signals he may lift ban on alcohol in football stands

author: Heather Stewart
description:
Wes Streeting says he leads a ‘ministry for growth’ as Labour seeks to show more defence spending will create UK jobs

Defence contractors have promised to create 40,000 apprenticeships, work experience placements and jobs for young people each year, as Wes Streeting claimed to be overseeing a “ministry for growth”.

Labour is keen to demonstrate that the rapid increase in defence spending planned for the coming years, which may necessitate tax rises, will result in jobs in the UK.

Continue reading...
title: UK defence contractors to offer 40,000 apprenticeships, placements and jobs

author: Harry Cockburn
description:
The Mercury prize-winner said ‘quite severe’ bleed was why he’d missed support slots with Mumford & Sons this year

The British singer-songwriter Michael Kiwanuka has said he has suffered a stroke and faces a “long tough journey” on the road to recovery.

The 39-year-old singer from London, whose hits include Cold Little Heart and Home Again, said the “quite severe” bleed in his brain was the reason he had missed some tour dates this year when he was due to support Mumford & Sons, and that the stroke had been brought on by high blood pressure.

Continue reading...
title: Michael Kiwanuka says he faces ‘long, tough journey’ to recovery from stroke

author: Martin Farrer
description:
An emotional prime minister says that Kyiv’s cause is ‘an issue for the world’ as he also sets out the need for a new global order

Anthony Albanese has announced Australia will provide $60m more in support for Ukraine’s fight against Russia’s invasion during an emotional meeting with Volodymyr ⁠Zelenskyy on the sidelines of the UN meeting in New York.

With the prime minister planning to use a key speech in New York to warn that the international world order was “no longer fit for purpose”, he hugged the Ukrainian president as the latter thanked Australia for its support.

Continue reading...
title: ‘My friend’: Anthony Albanese announces $60m more for Ukraine at Zelenskyy meeting

author: Patrick Butler Social policy editor
description:
Warning from Charity Commission for England and Wales concludes two-year investigation after death of Hisham al-Hakimi in October 2023

The international aid charity Save the Children has been issued with an official regulatory warning over management failures and misconduct that put staff at its Yemen office at serious risk.

The warning concluded a two-year investigation by the Charity Commission for England and Wales into the running of the office after the death of its safety and security director, Hisham al-Hakimi, in October 2023 after he was detained by the Yemeni authorities.

Continue reading...
title: Save the Children officially warned by regulator over staff put at risk in Yemen

author: Associated Press
description:
Ker’Sean Ramey, 41, set to die by lethal injection, sixth person to be executed by Texas officials this year

A man found guilty of fatally shooting three people during a 2005 attempted robbery at a rural Texas home is scheduled to be executed Wednesday, a week after the other man convicted in the killings was put to death.

Ker’Sean Ramey, 41, is set to die by lethal injection at the state penitentiary in Huntsville. He would be the sixth person executed so far this year in Texas, with three more scheduled.

Continue reading...
title: Texas to execute death-row prisoner over 2005 triple killing

author: Daniel Boffey Chief reporter
description:
Javier Milei says organisation is filled with ‘arrogant parasites’ and threatens to take ‘matters into our own hands’

Javier Milei has condemned the UN as he warned that Argentina would take “matters into our own hands” in its dispute with Britain over the sovereignty of the Falkland Islands.

In a caustic speech at the general assembly in New York, the Argentinian president criticised the UN for being ineffective when it comes to the long-running tensions over the British overseas territory in the south Atlantic known in Argentina as the Malvinas.

Continue reading...
title: Argentina president attacks UN over inaction on Falkland Islands sovereignty

author: Fiona Harvey Environment editor
description:
El Niño poses critical threat to nations’ defences, says Ed Miliband in presentation to global foreign ministers

The UK has warned countries around the world that the climate and nature crises and the coming El Niño threaten their national security and defence, presenting foreign ministries with the findings of an explosive report suppressed under Keir Starmer.

Ed Miliband, the foreign secretary, made a presentation to the foreign ministers of the EU as well as Kenya and other countries on Wednesday night at a private meeting during the UN general assembly in New York, based on the report by the UK’s spy chiefs that found the collapse of natural systems around the world would lead to conflict, migration and food shortages.
title: UK shares findings of damning climate crisis national security report suppressed under Starmer

author: Harry Cockburn
description:
Witness says T2 Hawk aircraft, which was being used for a training flight, ‘was basically on fire’ on takeoff

An RAF jet crashed and exploded moments after two pilots ejected during a training flight over Anglesey (Ynys Môn) in north Wales on Wednesday.

The aircraft, a Hawk T2, had just taken off from RAF Valley on the west of the island when the incident occurred, witnesses said.

Continue reading...
title: RAF jet crashes and explodes in Anglesey moments after pilots eject

author: Associated Press
description:
FBIjobs.gov offline on Wednesday as ShinyHunters group claims to have accessed records of agents and applicants

The FBI is investigating an apparent breach of its jobs website as a criminal hacking group claimed to have accessed “very sensitive data” on nearly all agents and job applicants.

“The FBI is aware of claims regarding unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and is currently investigating,” the bureau said in a statement. The website, the main portal for prospective employees to learn about the FBI and initiate the application process, remained offline Wednesday morning.

Continue reading...
title: FBI investigates breach of jobs website as hackers claim ‘very sensitive data’ stolen

author: Nils Pratley
description:
The biggest flotation in five years was a bit of a shoo-in. Let’s see what happens when overseas competition is tougher

  • Indian billionaire’s payments firm plots biggest London flotation in years

A win is a win, but we should probably contain our excitement about the biggest flotation in London for five years. Airtel Money, a payments processor that operates in 13 African countries and should be worth between £6bn and £7bn, is a welcome addition to the stock market but it would be a stretch to say the event marks a definitive change in the weather to end the listings drought.

Why? Because, in a sense, Airtel Money is already here. It is a 78%-owned subsidiary of Airtel Africa, an established F
title: Does Airtel Money mark the end of London’s listing drought? Not yet | Nils Pratley

author: Catie McLeod Consumer affairs reporter
description:
The price of a basket of items in Coles, Woolworths, IGA and Aldi increased to an average of $43.62, survey says

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Groceries have become more expensive at all four of Australia’s major supermarket chains, with the average price of a basket of essentials increasing by 7% between March and June, new analysis has found.

The consumer advocacy group Choice on Thursday released its 10th quarterly government-funded survey of supermarket prices, which it assessed by filling a basket with eight common grocery items at 104 different stores in June.
title: Groceries rise by 7% across Australian supermarket chains, Choice finds

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Researcher says public debate since May budget has overstated how much reforms will cost landlords and investors

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Most property investors may end up paying less capital gains tax after Labor’s budget reforms, research based on an analysis of historical data suggests.

The e61 Institute’s analysis also found half of all landlords would have faced higher costs from the loss of negative gearing over the period from 2008 to 2025 if the new system had been in place, suggesting the tax reforms alone cannot explain a
title: Property investors may pay less capital gains tax under Labor’s reforms, analysis suggests

author: Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: Australian Gas Infrastructure Group lobbying campaign warns energy bills could increase by $100 unless ban is reversed, despite experts disagreeing

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The gas industry has been accused of unleashing a “scare campaign” before the Victorian election as it pressures the state government to reverse a ban on gas in new homes.

A paper prepared by a lobbyist for the Australian Gas Infrastructure Group (AGIG) and shared with ministers has warned annual household gas bills could increase by $100 u
title: Gas lobby ‘scare campaign’ urges Victoria to scrap ban in new homes, leaked documents show

author: Benita Kolovos Victorian state correspondent
description:
Exclusive: ‘We don’t want to see any winding back of women’s rights,’ health minister says ahead of state election

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Victorian Labor government is announcing new measures to improve access to medical abortion, as it puts reproductive rights on the election agenda and claims One Nation could use abortion as a negotiating chip with the Coalition in the event of a hung parliament.

On Thursday, the deputy premier and minister for women, Gabrielle Williams, and the health minister, Ingrid Stitt, will announce a rollout of new portable ultrasound machines for the state’s 20 sexual and reproductive health hubs.
title: Victorian Labor puts reproductive rights on election agenda as it warns One Nation could try to wind back abortion access

author: Patrick Commins
description:
Housing costs are up with renters worst affected and financial stress is also growing, according to the largest survey of its type

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Every year, thousands of Australians answer a series of questions as part of the long-running Hilda survey.

This questionnaire – more expansively known as the household, income and labour dynamics in Australia survey – has been tracking the same households since 2001.

Patrick Commins is Guardian Australia’s economics editor

Continue reading...
title: Young Australians are staying in the family home for longer – and it’s not hard to see why

author: Ariana Baio in Washington
description:
Justice department cites national security to support ban on CNN, Politico and MS Now as trio file lawsuit in response

  • US politics live – latest updates

The US Department of Justice has defended Donald Trump’s decision to ban three new organizations from the White House, arguing in a court filing that access to the grounds was a “privilege” and citing national security concerns.

Lawyers for the US president doubled down on Trump’s claims about CNN, Politico and MS Now reporting “Fake News”, and insisted the ban did not violate the first amendment because “access to t
title: DoJ defends Trump media ban: ‘Access to the White House is a privilege’

author: Matthew Pearce
description:
Author Russell Warfield argues the Green leader’s brand of politics is not new but has evolved in the party over time

Watermelons: the term used to describe the members of the Green party of England and Wales who are green on the outside and red on the inside. People in this faction are environmentalists, but when you cut them open, they bleed socialist ideologies.

Of the roughly 160,000 people that have flocked to the party since Zack Polanski became leader last year, most are thought to be in this camp, drawn to a political space on the left that they see as vacated by the Labour party.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Watermelons’: Zack Polanski and the rise of the ‘green outside, red inside’ eco-populists

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
Administration is holding back Covid vaccines for all children in at least 11 states and one US territory

The Trump administration is holding back Covid vaccines for all children in at least 11 states and one US territory, and officials have not indicated when or whether the shots will become available.

It’s the latest step by top officials to restrict vaccines in America – and it sets a precedent for holding back other immunizations, experts said.

Continue reading...
title: Delays in Covid shots for kids is latest bid by Trump officials to restrict vaccines

author: Associated Press
description:
Criminal investigation could include manslaughter or negligent homicide charges after 27 flood deaths last year

Camp Mystic faces a criminal investigation that could include manslaughter or negligent homicide charges in the deaths of 27 girls amid devastating flooding in Texas last year, court documents show.

In applications for search warrants executed last week, investigators sought to obtain the electronic communications of the camp’s owners, saying they could provide evidence of manslaughter, negligent homicide, child abandonment or other crimes. No charges have been brought, and a representative of the camp did not immediately return messages seeking comment.

Continue reading...
title: Camp Mystic faces investigation as Texas Rangers seek evidence of manslaughter

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Tories say deal should be fully scrapped after it was criticised by Donald Trump during his meeting with Andy Burnham


Chagos Islands deal ‘can’t go ahead’ without US support, Streeting says

The former Labour minister leading the government’s review into youth unemployment has written to 100 firms to ask them to provide work placements and jobs for young people, the Press Association reports. PA says:

Alan Milburn, who was commissioned by former prime minister Keir Starmer to lead the government’s review into worklessness, has approached “business leaders” in sectors including rail, transport and utilities to ask them to provide more chances for young people.

The Milburn review said Royal Mail, Octopus Energy, Greene King and Lloyds bank are among the companies who are already offering opportunities to school and university leavers
title: Streeting confirms annual £120m payments to Mauritius on hold while Chagos Islands deal is reviewed – UK politics live

author: Agence France-Presse in Paris
description:
Discovery of Gallo-Roman period structure hailed as ‘major breakthrough’ by French culture ministry

An ancient wall discovered beneath Paris has been described as a “major breakthrough” by France’s culture ministry, with the archaeological find possibly confirming the location of the city’s original settlement.

A roughly 20-metre (65ft) stretch of wall dating from the Gallo-Roman period was discovered in Paris this summer beneath a building on the Île de la Cité, near Notre Dame Cathedral in the heart of the French capital.

Continue reading...
title: Ancient wall found beneath Paris could confirm site of first settlement

author: Martin Belam
description:
US-Iran meeting takes place on sidelines despite president’s threat to ‘annihilate’ Tehran regime. Plus, one man’s month-long pilates odyssey

Good morning. Donald Trump has used the platform of the UN general assembly in New York to threaten to “annihilate the Islamic republic” of Iran, “and do it quickly”. He called on countries to unite to isolate Tehran and bring down global energy prices.

Despite his bombastic rhetoric, Trump also said Iranian officials held three hours of talks with the US special envoy Steve Witkoff on the sidelines of the meeting. Witkoff said he felt very good about the meeting, the first such contact since the US-vice-president, JD Vance, met an Iranian delegation in Switzer
title: Trump addresses UN with mixture of boasts, threats and jibes | First Thing

author: Stephen Burgen in Barcelona
description:
Housing rights campaigners decry landlord’s ‘barbaric behaviour’ after apartment Maricarmen had lived in for 71 years was bought by a developer

There were violent scenes in Madrid on Wednesday as riot police fought with protesters trying to prevent the eviction of a disabled 87-year-old woman from her apartment in the El Retiro district of the city.

Hundreds of protesters had gathered, many of them overnight, in an effort to block the fourth attempt to carry out the eviction. Activists from the Madrid and Barcelona tenants’ union, and celebrities including the actor Carlos Bardem and the singer and actor Ana Belén, also joined the protest.

Continue reading...
title: Police use teargas on protesters as disabled woman, 87, evicted from Madrid home

author: Dan Milmo Global technology editor
description:
Ofcom says site’s age-checking regime may not be ‘highly effective’, as required by the Online Safety Act

One of the world’s most visited pornography websites is being investigated by the UK’s communications watchdog over concerns it can still be accessed by children.

Pornhub’s age checking regime may not be “highly effective”, according to Ofcom, and could be in breach of online safety laws requiring strict measures to prevent under-18s from accessing sexually explicit content.

Continue reading...
title: UK watchdog investigating Pornhub over concerns it can still be accessed by children

author: Penry Buckley
description:
Sharangan Maheswaran also told inquiry his bid for story on unsubstantiated rumour about then-Liberal minister David Elliott was ‘not a serious offer’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A purported $5m extortion attempt of fugitive property developer Jean Nassif was actually a genuine request for his company Toplace to pay a contractor, a lawyer assisting the New South Wales anti-corruption watchdog has argued.

Former Toplace lawyer and executive Sharangan Maheswaran told the Independent Commiss
title: A ‘grubby rumour’ and a $5m extortion attempt: former Toplace executive gives Icac evidence

author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
description:
NHS England initiative to reduce cut-off period to three months ‘disproportionately affecting’ most deprived areas

An NHS policy to remove “ghost patients” from GP lists is inadvertently leaving some of the poorest people in England without vital healthcare, analysis has found.

Under previous NHS rules, inactive patients at risk of being removed from their GP practice were given six months to respond to outreach. But under NHS England’s accelerated list validation timeline, introduced last October, patients now have only three months to reply.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Ghost patient’ policy wrongly removing at-risk people from GP lists, doctors say

author: Achol Arok and Ima Caldwell
description:
This blog is now closed

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Andrew Bragg, the shadow housing minister, said he believes in “big debates” about housing after pushing his new proposal yesterday to allow people to use their superannuation as collateral to get a home loan.

The policy hasn’t been adopted by the opposition, and leader Angus Taylor said yesterday it wasn’t Coalition policy.

We’re a great country, and we should be able to have big debates, as we had in the 80s and 90s about national savings and housing and the like, which led, in fact, to the super guarantee. …

It’s very important that we look to calibrate the retirement and housing and superannuation systems to make
title: Shoebridge says US submission on online safety laws an ‘extraordinary intervention’ – as it happened

author: Tory Shepherd
description:
No trace of Gus has been found since he went missing from his family’s South Australian farm on 27 September last year

The parents of missing four-year-old Gus Lamont have made an emotional plea for any information about their “unique little boy” as authorities offered a $1m reward over the disappearance.

No trace of Gus has been found since he went missing from his family’s enormous sheep farm in the South Australian outback almost a year ago.

Continue reading...
title: Gus Lamont’s parents make emotional plea as $1m reward offered for information about disappearance

author: Kat Wong
description:
Friend sobs in witness box and tells Sydney murder trial Baird was scared to go to the police

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Before he was fatally shot, Jesse Baird became “petrified” of Beau Lamarre and kept repeating that the police officer had a gun, a court has heard.

Lamarre-Condon has been accused of fatally shooting Sydney couple Jesse Baird, 26, and Luke Davies, 29, with a police service weapon at Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
title: Jesse Baird ‘petrified’ of Beau Lamarre-Condon and kept repeating ‘he has a gun’, court hears

author: Sarah Basford Canales and Petra Stock
description:
Several measures were previously introduced or supported by Coalition, prompting claim Liberals and Nationals would ‘let climate change rip’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Angus Taylor has vowed to repeal a raft of emissions reduction and renewable energy policies, including several measures supported by or introduced under past Coalition governments, within a month of being elected prime minister, prompting accusations he would “let climate change rip”.

On Wednesday, Taylor’s energy spokesp
title: Angus Taylor pledges to repeal swathe of climate policies, saying ‘Australia has done its bit’
